stem.text: Which compound would give positive tests with alkaline I<sub>2</sub>(aq) and with Fehling’s reagent?

stem.alt: Four skeletal formulas labelled A to D. A: a cyclohexane ring with a ring C=O (ketone) at one position and a CHO (aldehyde) group on the opposite ring carbon. B: a cyclohexane ring with two ring C=O groups opposite each other and an exocyclic =CH2 on the carbon next to one of them. C: a cyclopentane ring with a ring C=O, and on another ring carbon a C(=O)CH3 (methyl ketone) group. D: a cyclobutane ring with a CHO group on one carbon and a C(=O)CH3 group on the neighbouring carbon.

explanation.text: Fehling’s reagent gives a red-brown precipitate only with aldehydes, so the compound must contain a CHO group. Alkaline I<sub>2</sub>(aq) gives a yellow tri-iodomethane precipitate only with a CH<sub>3</sub>CO– group (or a CH<sub>3</sub>CH(OH)– group), so the compound must also contain a methyl ketone.
A ketone C=O that is part of a ring is not a CH<sub>3</sub>CO– group, because the carbonyl carbon is bonded to two ring carbons rather than to a CH<sub>3</sub>.

optionAnalysis.text: Has a CHO group (positive with Fehling’s), but its ketone is in the ring, so there is no CH<sub>3</sub>CO– group for the iodoform test.
Has two ring ketones and no CHO or CH<sub>3</sub>CO– group, so both tests are negative.
Has a CH<sub>3</sub>CO– group (positive iodoform) but no aldehyde, so the Fehling’s test is negative.
Has both a CHO group (Fehling’s positive) and a CH<sub>3</sub>CO– group (tri-iodomethane positive).

reasoningChain: Fehling’s positive needs an aldehyde: A and D.
Alkaline I<sub>2</sub> positive needs CH<sub>3</sub>CO–: C and D.
Only D has both: option D.

inferredMistakes.text: Treating any ketone as a positive iodoform test and choosing A, which has a ring C=O but no CH<sub>3</sub>CO– group.
